harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as an authoritative Kea DHCP server on the private eth1 network (192.168.50.0/24) shared with node2 and node3, and configured node2/node3 (Alpine) to obtain their eth1 address via DHCP instead of static assignment, entirely via an Ansible playbook (/root/ansible/site.yml) run from the cluster control node (node4). Node2 leased 192.168.50.101/24 and node3 leased 192.168.50.100/24 from node1's DHCP server (192.168.50.1). All four managed nodes were then restarted one at a time via their native reboot mechanism, with proven boot_id changes and verified post-restart recovery of DHCP service, leases, and Ansible manageability (SSH access persisted via VyOS's own config system).
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes: node1=VyOS router (eth0=platform net, eth1=private net to node2/3), node2/node3=Alpine clients (eth0=platform net, eth1=private net, initially down/unaddressed), node4=Ubuntu control node with ansible-core preinstalled

Established SSH key access from node4 to node1 (vyos user), node2 (alpine user), node3 (alpine user) using node4's own SSH keypair; granted passwordless sudo to the alpine users via /etc/sudoers.d/alpine
Installed python3 on node2/node3 via apk (required for Ansible modules)
Built an Ansible project on node4 (/root/ansible: inventory.ini, ansible.cfg, site.yml, files/vyos-configure-dhcp.sh)

Debugged VyOS CLI automation quirks: non-root config session establishment silently fails for the vyos user over non-interactive SSH unless invoked via sudo as a plain command (not Ansible become/pty); removed 'set -e' which aborted on benign non-zero returns inside VyOS vendor scripts; added required Kea DHCP subnet-id

Ran the Ansible playbook: router play sets eth1 static address 192.168.50.1/24 and configures an authoritative Kea DHCP server (shared-network LAN1, subnet 192.168.50.0/24, range .100-.200); clients play adds an eth1 DHCP stanza to /etc/network/interfaces and brings up a DHCP lease via ifup
Verified node2 obtained 192.168.50.101/24 and node3 obtained 192.168.50.100/24 via DHCP from node1
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, service state, DHCP leases) on all 4 nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time using native reboot, polling until each came back, confirming boot_id changed each time
Verified DHCP server config and kea-dhcp4 listener survived node1's restart (persisted via VyOS config.boot save)
Verified node2 and node3 automatically re-acquired their DHCP leases from node1 after their own restarts
Persisted the vyos user's SSH public key via VyOS's own 'system login user vyos authentication public-keys' config (since ad hoc /home/vyos/.ssh changes do not survive VyOS's live-image reboot)
Re-ran the full Ansible playbook after all 4 restarts to confirm idempotent success end-to-end (all config already-applied, both clients still holding correct DHCP leases)

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as DHCP server on private network shared with node2/node3
evidence.summary: Ansible playbook run shows router play applying eth1=192.168.50.1/24 and Kea DHCP server config; direct verification shows kea-dhcp4 listening on 192.168.50.1:67 and committed dhcp-server config for subnet 192.168.50.0/24

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 obtain private-network address via DHCP instead of static assignment
evidence.summary: Ansible clients play adds 'iface eth1 inet dhcp' to /etc/network/interfaces and runs ifup; node2 shows dynamic lease 192.168.50.101/24, node3 shows dynamic lease 192.168.50.100/24

evidence.requirement: Implemented using Ansible from the control node
evidence.summary: ansible-playbook connectivity check, syntax check, and two full successful runs (initial apply and post-restart idempotent re-run) executed from node4 using inventory.ini targeting node1/node2/node3

evidence.requirement: node1 baseline capture and restart with proof of changed boot identity and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 50503c5d... captured with healthy DHCP service; reboot issued; connection timeout confirms outage; new boot_id 80810335... confirms restart; post-restart check shows eth1 address and kea-dhcp4 listener recovered from persisted config.boot

evidence.requirement: node2 baseline capture and restart with proof of changed boot identity and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 198d7145... captured with active DHCP lease; reboot issued; connection reset confirms outage; new boot_id 56443087... confirms restart; post-restart check shows DHCP lease 192.168.50.101/24 automatically re-acquired

evidence.requirement: node3 baseline capture and restart with proof of changed boot identity and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 3760fa67... captured with active DHCP lease; reboot issued; connection reset confirms outage; new boot_id 7a76beef... confirms restart; post-restart check shows DHCP lease 192.168.50.100/24 automatically re-acquired

evidence.requirement: node4 (control node) baseline capture and restart with proof of changed boot identity and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 6fd57414... captured with Ansible project present; reboot issued; new boot_id 06113e02... confirms restart; Ansible project files intact post-restart; full playbook re-run from node4 afterward succeeds end-to-end, proving control-node functionality recovered
